summary: Emergency contacts for Nigeria: Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt. Nigeria's private hospital sector has improved significantly. Know these numbers before you arrive.

police.description: Nigeria Police Force emergency line (also works from mobile)
police.notes: Also try 199 from NTEL/MTN or the Lagos Emergency Management Agency at 767 (for Lagos State). Response quality varies significantly. For serious security incidents in Lagos, the Rapid Response Squad (RRS) can be more responsive.

ambulance.description: Federal Road Safety Corps and Emergency Medical Services
ambulance.notes: Lagos Emergency: 767. LASAMBUS (Lagos State Ambulance Service): +234 1 7944444. Private ambulances from hospitals like Reddington or Eko Hospital are often faster. 112 is the main national number.

fire.description: Lagos State Fire Service via 112 or 01-7652348
fire.notes: Lagos Fire Service direct: 01-7652348. Abuja Fire Service: 09-8701391. Response times outside major cities can be slow.

tourist.notes: Available during business hours for general tourist assistance.

embassies.name: U.S. Embassy Abuja
embassies.address: Plot 1075 Diplomatic Drive, Central District Area, Abuja
embassies.emergencyNote: Call main number and follow prompts for after-hours citizen emergency services

embassies.name: U.S. Consulate General Lagos
embassies.address: 2 Walter Carrington Crescent, Victoria Island, Lagos
embassies.emergencyNote: After-hours emergencies routed via main number and duty officer

embassies.name: British High Commission Abuja
embassies.address: Plot 1137, IBB Way, Maitama District, Abuja
embassies.emergencyNote: Call main number for after-hours emergency recording and duty officer access

embassies.name: Canadian High Commission Abuja
embassies.emergencyNote: Ottawa Emergency Watch and Response Centre for after-hours citizen emergencies

hospitals.name: Reddington Hospital
hospitals.address: 12 Catholic Mission Street, Victoria Island, Lagos
hospitals.notes: One of Lagos's top private hospitals. Full emergency services, ICU, and specialist care. Accepts major international insurance. Preferred by diaspora and expatriates in Victoria Island.

hospitals.name: Eko Hospital
hospitals.address: 31 Mobolaji Bank Anthony Way, Ikeja, Lagos
hospitals.notes: Leading private hospital in Ikeja, Lagos. 24-hour emergency, ICU, medical evacuation support. Accredited and well-equipped. Good for the airport area and mainland.

hospitals.name: Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH)
hospitals.notes: Main academic hospital for Lagos. Handles serious emergencies but can be severely overcrowded. Best used as a last resort or for specialized cases only.

hospitals.name: Nisa Premier Hospital
hospitals.notes: Top private hospital in Abuja. Used by the diplomatic community and government officials. Full emergency and specialist care. Accepts international insurance.

insurance.nhis: Nigeria's National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) is primarily for employed Nigerians. Visitors and diaspora should not rely on it. Private hospital care is affordable by international standards but payment is typically required upfront without insurance.
insurance.recommendation: Carry travel insurance with direct billing capability at private hospitals. Many Nigerian private hospitals require payment upfront and will reimburse via insurance later. Confirm your insurer has direct billing relationships in Nigeria. Medical evacuation to South Africa or Europe is recommended for serious long-term care.

keyAlerts: Dial 112 for all emergencies. This is the universal number across networks
In Lagos, 767 connects to the state emergency management agency
Private hospitals require upfront payment or insurance proof at admission. Carry documentation.
The U.S. has both an Embassy in Abuja and a Consulate in Lagos. Use the Lagos number if you are in the Southwest
Traffic in Lagos is severe. In a medical emergency, calling an Uber or private vehicle may be faster than waiting for ambulance
